title: Diego de Ibarra, Paris, 10 July 1593, in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher (BnF fr. 3984 no. 68)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's Spanish page fetched as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: his key tables are images, and two of them cover exactly the folios this entry cites.

The catalogue's piece numbers resolved to folios through the BnF depouillement, and the folio-to-canvas map for fr. 3983 and fr. 3984 built by reading folio numbers off top strips and interpolating; all four leaves located.
No. 68's figures run far higher and the leaf carries three-letter word groups, so it is the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, as Tomokiyo's citation of f. 145 says, not the cipher of the other three.

No. 68 read from deskewed strips with keyM.tsv (Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table): the clear opening and the first cipher lines (the other three letters read the same day with the office key, sessa1593).
The obvious candidate for the missing Feria-Mansfeld nomenclature, fr. 3995 f. 101, fetched and excluded: it is an Italian nomenclature belonging to another correspondence.

no. 68 line 11 transcribed and decoded with keyM.tsv as a test: syllables but no Spanish (va le ri a no la vi o xur que le de di as se ri as ...), as on lines 7-10. Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table gives no continuous text on the body, and the nomenclature is missing; lines 12-31 were not transcribed. (Superseded the same day: the failure came from truncated transcriptions; see the next steps.)
no. 68 transcribed in full from a 3600-px crop: 20 cipher lines, 598 groups (ct68.txt); the earlier 28-line estimate was wrong.

keyM decode of ct68.txt scored with the es-golden-age 5-gram (no spaces): -2.500 per character against a maximum of -3.378 for 200 value-shuffled keys. Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table is real on this leaf and gives Spanish (a mi no me parece que puede, todo lo que se puede, pareceria que venia a ayudar, no estamos desesperados).
Unconstrained hill-climb of all numbers (anneal68.py) collapsed onto que (score -1.59, nonsense); rejected.

Constrained fill of the numbers missing from keyM (fill68.py): 57 = li accepted (top candidate, gain far above median; peligro, aliento). 64 (ha by context) not separated from na by the LM, left unread; 31, 77, 81, 95 and the 200/800 T groups undetermined. Cribs Feria, Mansfeld, Liga fit no syllable run; Paris and Su Magestad are in clear.
no. 68 scored for sense: 224/598. The new value belongs to the Mansfeld cipher, so the doubtful groups of nos. 45/79/47 (office key) gained nothing.

Entry split from sessa1593 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 68 is in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, not the office cipher of nos. 45/79/47. Files moved; dec68.py rerun with fill68.json (598 tokens); sense rows moved to sense68.tsv: 224/598.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): ct68.txt; texts/no68_decryption.md is the saved output of dec68.py with fill68.json (all 20 cipher lines), reading68.md the earlier hand reading of ll. 4-10; key keyM.tsv + fill68.json.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/no68_decryption.md and reading68.md read: the decode is a stream of syllables with the three-letter word codes unread in most clauses; a few phrases are intelligible, no sentence can be built (docs/_check_reading.py: 0 of 3 and 14 of 30 sentences clean, the clean ones mostly the clear opening). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key work kept as a part); fraction_read 0.375 -> 0.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld key, which cites this folio, applied (read with known key, recorded under parts), decodes the syllabic figures, but the three-letter word codes that carry much of the sense have no table, and the letter does not build sentences.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the one document does not build sentences, so nothing counts as read (0). Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.375, sense68.tsv (224 of 598 groups of ct68.txt marked as forming Spanish sense), which counted phrases scattered among unread codes.
outcome.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from sessa1593. The syllables read; the three-letter word codes, which carry much of the sense, have no published table.

gaps.detail: the three-letter nomenclature (pra, dur, hes, gar, pun, rom, mon, xen, vul, cil, var, vis, tor ...) is published nowhere and no crib fixes it; numbers 64, 31, 77, 81, 95 not separated by the LM control; diacritic finals dropped in ct68.txt

texts.label: Diego de Ibarra, Paris, 10 July 1593, BnF fr. 3984 no. 68, f. 145
texts.summary: Ibarra writes from Paris during the Estates of 1593 in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher: the messenger he is despatching, cavalry awaited, 'no estamos desesperados', peril, and help that might come with the cavalry. The three-letter word codes, which carry much of the sense, have no published table and stay unread.
texts.note: The decode is a stream of syllables with the three-letter word codes, which carry much of the sense, unread ('to do s a lo so de o di a quo u y no co ti nu a [pra] e s la de'); only a few phrases are intelligible and lines 7-10 do not give continuous Spanish (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

parts.label: no. 68 (Feria-Mansfeld key applied; text decoded, not read)
parts.basis: Tomokiyo's Feria-Mansfeld table (keyM.tsv) plus 57 = li gives Spanish syllables against a shuffled-key control; the three-letter word codes are unread, so the decode has holes in nearly every sentence. Decoded, not read (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).
